taxonomyNote: NatureServe: formerly (AOU 1983, 1998) placed in Francolinus; genetic data indicate Francolinus is not monophyletic. ADW still files it as Francolinus pondicerianus.
fieldMarks: About a foot long, distinct rows of brown feathers with a pale face and throat
Sexes look similar; males may be slightly larger
behavior: Loud call often heard in the morning
Common in dry areas; easily seen near lawns and roads at dawn and dusk (Hawaii)
habitat: Common in dry areas; easily found near hotel lawns and near roads at dawn and dusk.
range: Native to India; introduced to Hawaii. NatureServe records it in Hawaii.
